The PR validates `.git` ancestors before selecting the portable runtime path and adds an init-to-sync regression test for local databases beneath unrelated Git metadata.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current behavior classifies a missing local database beneath any `.git` ancestor as portable, causing sync to mirror a source database that does not yet exist. A live current-main run was not available during this review.

target.title: fix(sync): allow local databases under stray Git metadata
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `gitcrawl init --db ...` followed by `gitcrawl sync` failed with `stat portable source db: no such file or directory` when an ancestor of the database path contained a stray `.git` directory that was not a Git worktree.

Gitcrawl treated the path as a portable-store checkout and tried to copy the not-yet-created local database into a runtime mirror.

## Why This Change Was Made

Portable-store discovery now verifies candidate `.git` ancestors with Git before selecting the portable runtime path. Valid Git worktrees keep their existing behavior, including portable stores created before Gitcrawl added its checkout marker.

## User Impact

Users can initialize and sync a local database below directories containing unrelated or incomplete Git metadata. Existing portable-store checkouts continue to use their writable runtime mirrors.

## Evidence

- Added `TestSyncCreatesLocalDatabaseBelowUnrelatedGitMetadata`, which runs the complete `init` then `sync` flow against a test GitHub server and verifies that the requested database contains the synced thread.
- `make test-coverage` — passes, total coverage 85.0%.
- `go vet ./...`
- `go mod tidy` with no `go.mod` or `go.sum` diff.
- `go build -ldflags '-X github.com/openclaw/gitcrawl/internal/cli.version=pr-test' -o bin/gitcrawl ./cmd/gitcrawl`
- `./scripts/test-release.sh`
